column2: AI education 2026 adoption regulation state bills players
column3: Trackers DISAGREE on volume and the spread is the datum: 134 bills / 31 states, 77 bills / 27 states, and 52 bills / 25 states for Q1.  Themes are consistent across all three: student-data privacy (California AB 1159 barring student data from model training), human-in-the-loop (Oklahoma SB 1734 barring AI as the main basis for grading or discipline, with a parental opt-out), AI literacy in statute (Alabama HB 329 making an AI-inclusive CS course a graduation requirement), governance capacity (Maryland SB 720 requiring district AI policies and AI coordinators).  Two opposite poles: New York A.9190 would prohibit classroom AI below grade 9; Utah SB 322 establishes a red-team SANDBOX.  Ohio set a hard deadline — every K-12 district to adopt a formal AI policy by July 1.

column1: EMEA
column2: AI education 2026 adoption EU AI Act AI literacy players
column3: The AILit framework (European Commission + OECD) was presented 2026-06-17/18 and defines AI literacy for primary and secondary schooling in FOUR domains and NINETEEN competences, built with CodeAI (formerly Code.org) from a consultation of 2 000+ contributors.  It is NON-BINDING and will inform PISA 2029.  It sits on top of the Article 4 AI-literacy duty, binding on every organisation using AI systems — therefore every school — since 2025-02-02.  Annex III high-risk duties for education are reported at 2027-12-02, deferred from 2026-08-02 by the Digital Omnibus.  An EACEA call (deadline 2026-09-20) is recruiting a squad to map AI literacy across Member States' schools and teacher education, running 2026-10 → 2027-01.  🔴 Sources CONFLICT on whether the Omnibus altered Article 4: one reads it as replaced by a duty to "support the development of" AI literacy, another says Article 4 is unchanged.  This base publishes NEITHER reading.

column1: APAC
column3: Education is in STATUTE here rather than in guidance: South Korea's AI Basic Act in force since 2026-01-22 is the region's first comprehensive mandatory AI law, and Vietnam's took effect 2026-03-01.  China has no general AI law but enforceable specifics — AI-content labelling, and model filing covering 988 services as of 2026-06-30.  India has no dedicated AI statute and governs through its data-protection rules, phasing to May 2027, while making AI and computational thinking COMPULSORY from Class 3 in the 2026-27 academic year under the IndiaAI Mission.  China is reported to have made AI compulsory from age six.  Japan's AI Promotion Act carries no fines and no prohibitions.  Ipsos Education Monitor 2026: Asian markets show LOWER support for banning AI in schools than for restricting children's social media, while Australia and New Zealand show higher support for a ban.
column4: search-channel convergence.  The curriculum mandate and the statute dates come from secondary trackers; no ministry host was reached

column1: LATAM
column3: The strongest adoption numbers this base holds for any region, and they are DEMAND rather than supply: UNESCO reports NINE IN TEN 15-year-olds across the 13 regional countries in PISA 2025 have already used AI chatbots for schoolwork, and TALIS 2024 puts secondary teachers' AI use at 56 % in Brazil and 55 % in Chile against an OECD average of 36 %.  Regulation is still prospective everywhere: Brazil's PL 2338/2023 is in process and its high-risk category EXPLICITLY INCLUDES education, which would bring mandatory impact assessments to schools and universities; Chile's bill is pending and principles-based; Mexico's 2026 changes cover deepfakes, performers' rights and enforcement — NOT education — and sources disagree whether they amount to a general AI law.  Tec de Monterrey is redesigning 44+ degree programmes to integrate AI.
column4: search-channel convergence.  unesco.org and the regional observatory hosts do not resolve; the PISA and TALIS figures are quoted from UNESCO's summary page as relayed by the search channel, not read at source
